title: Flip a Bit
statement:
Flip one bit of a number: a 0 bit becomes 1 and a 1 bit becomes 0. Bits are counted from the right, starting at 0, so bit 0 is the lowest bit. Then report whether that bit is set in the new number.

The input is two integers `n` and `k` on one line, separated by a space, where `0 <= n <= 1000000000` and `0 <= k <= 29`. Print two lines. The first line is `n` with bit `k` flipped. The second line is `true` when bit `k` is 1 in the new number and `false` when it is 0. For example, 5 is `101` in binary, and flipping bit 1 gives `111`, which is 7.

Input:

```text
5 1
```

Expected output:

```text
7
true
```
hints: `1 << k` is a mask with only bit `k` set.
XOR with a mask flips exactly the bits that are 1 in the mask. AND with the same mask tells you whether that bit is set.
